sources.title: Alaska proposal could tighten access to state records in Juneau
sources.outlet: Juneau Empire, Jeffrey Kennett, November 14th (news, the only outlet reporting the draft's provisions)
sources.note: Reports the Department of Administration draft: no requests through third party services or automated tools including AI, forms or portals, 250 document or 15 hour stop, all hours past five, appeal 60 to 30 working days, resident priority. Gives no reason for the AI clause, no deadline, no named official.

sources.title: Notice of Proposed Changes On Alaska Public Records Act Regulations (notice 225838, listed November 11th)
sources.outlet: State of Alaska Online Public Notices, Department of Administration (primary, listing only; notice body returned 403)
sources.note: Confirms the notice's title, agency and date.

sources.title: 2 AAC 96.310, 96.325 and 96.340 (current Alaska public records regulations)
sources.outlet: Alaska Administrative Code via Cornell LII (primary regulation text)
sources.note: Oral requests are valid, no denial solely for skipping the form, 10 working days to respond, 60 working days to appeal.

sources.title: AS 40.25.110 and AS 40.25.120 (Alaska Public Records Act)
sources.outlet: Alaska Statutes via FindLaw (primary statute text)
sources.note: Fee trigger past five person hours a month; every person has a right to inspect a public record, with exceptions.
